17.1. Taxiway/Taxilane Safety Area (TSA)
        A Taxiway Safety Area is a defined surface alongside the taxiway prepared or suitable for reducing the risk
        of damage to an airplane unintentionally departing the taxiway (see AC 150/5300-13, latest edition).
        Construction activities within the TSA are subject to the following conditions:


    NV5/WHPacific, Inc.
    BCRAA: Del Norte County Regional Airport           CSPP     Runway 18-36 Rehabilitation, Marking and Lighting Project
                                                        11
        a)   No construction may occur within the TSA while the taxiway is open for aircraft operations. The TSA
             dimensions may be temporarily adjusted if the taxiway is restricted to aircraft operations requiring a
             TSA that is equal to the TSA width available during construction (see AC 150/5300-13, Table 4-1).
        b) The airport operator must coordinate the adjustment of the TSA width as permitted above with the
           appropriate FAA Airports Regional or District Office and the FAA air traffic manager and issue a
           NOTAM.
        c)   The CSPP and SPCD must provide procedures for ensuring adequate distance for protection from
             blasting operations.
        d) Excavations.
             Open trenches or excavations are not permitted within the TSA while the taxiway is open. If possible,
             backfill trenches before the taxiway is opened. If the taxiway must be opened before excavations are
             backfilled, cover the excavations appropriately. Covering for open trenches must be designed to allow
             the safe operation of the heaviest aircraft operating on the taxiway across the trench without damage to
             the aircraft.

             Construction contractors must prominently mark open trenches and excavations at the construction site
             with red or orange flags, as approved by the airport operator, and light them with red lights during
             hours of restricted visibility or darkness.

        e)   Erosion Control.
             Soil erosion must be controlled to maintain TSA standards, that is, the TSA must be cleared and
             graded and have no potentially hazardous ruts, humps, depressions, or other surface variations, and
             capable, under dry conditions, of supporting snow removal equipment, aircraft rescue and firefighting
             equipment, and the occasional passage of aircraft without causing structural damage to the aircraft.
17.2. Taxiway/Taxilane Object Free Area (TOFA)
        Unlike the Runway Object Free Area, aircraft wings regularly penetrate the taxiway object free area during
        normal operations, thus the restrictions are more stringent. Except as provided below, no construction may
        occur within the TOFA while the taxiway is open for aircraft operations.

        The TOFA dimensions may be temporarily adjusted if the taxiway is restricted to aircraft operations
        requiring a taxiway object free area that is equal to the taxiway object free area width available.

        Offset taxiway pavement markings may be used as a temporary measure to provide the required taxiway
        object free area. Where offset taxiway pavement markings are provided, centerline lighting or reflectors are
        required.

        Construction activity may be accomplished without adjusting the width of the taxiway object free area,
        subject to the following restrictions:

        b) Appropriate NOTAMs are issued.
        c)   Marking and lighting meeting the provisions of section 16 above are implemented.
        d) Five-foot clearance is maintained between equipment and materials and any part of an aircraft
           (includes wingtip overhang). In these situations, flaggers must be used to direct construction
           equipment, and wing walkers will be necessary to guide aircraft. Wing walkers should be
           airline/aviation personnel rather than construction workers. If such clearance can only be maintained if
           an aircraft does not have full use of the entire taxiway width (with its main landing gear at the edge of
           the pavement), then it will be necessary to move personnel and equipment for the passage of that
           aircraft.

18. Other Limitations on Construction
18.1. Prohibitions




    NV5/WHPacific, Inc.
    BCRAA: Del Norte County Regional Airport           CSPP      Runway 18-36 Rehabilitation, Marking and Lighting Project
                                                        12
        Prior to the start of construction, the Contractor shall provide the Sponsor with specific equipment heights
        in order to complete FAA form 7460-1 and submit for FAA airspace review. A determination letter from
        the FAA acknowledging the equipment heights within the project area is required before construction can
        commence.
        a)   No use of open flame welding or torches unless fire safety precautions are provided and the airport
             operator has approved their use.
        b) No use of electrical blasting caps on or within 1,000 feet of the airport property.
        c)   No use of flare pots within the Airport Operations Area (AOA).
        d) No smoking within the AOA.
18.2. Other Restrictions
        Prior to start of construction, the Contractor shall provide the Port with specific equipment heights or FAA
        airspace review. A determination letter from the FAA acknowledging equipment height within the project
        area is required before construction can commence.

 TO:               Border Coast Regional Airport Authority Board of Commissioners

 FROM:             Ryan Cooley, Airport Director

 SUBJECT:          Tolowa Dee-Ni’ Nation Land Acknowledgement Recognition and Acknowledgement


INTRODUCTION:
Review, consider and provide guidance on proposed Tolowa Dee-ni’ Nation Land Acknowledgement.**

SUMMARY/DISCUSSION:
In light of the fact that the Del Norte County Regional Airport is located on the ancestral homelands of the Tolowa people, Mrs. Emily
Reed – Public Relations Manager for the Tolowa Dee-ni’ Nation has inquired about the possibility and willingness of the Border Coast
Regional Airport Authority to officially acknowledge the location. This may be accomplished by creating and placing a plaque in the
passenger terminal or a create and display a permanent declaration on the electronic displays throughout the passenger terminal, as
well as on the official flycrescentcity.com website.

Sample verbiage:

“The Border Coast Regional Airport Authority hereby recognizes that the Del Norte County Regional Airport is located on the ancestral
homelands of the Tolowa people, who have stewarded this land throughout the generations. We acknowledge that this land has a
traditional name, Taa-ghii~-'a~ located in the Taa-'at-dvn district. The Border Coast Regional Airport Authority recognizes and respects
the enduring relationship that has existed between the many Indigenous peoples and their homelands since time immemorial.”



ALTERNATIVES:
Do not move forward with a formal land acknowledgement
Provide airport staff with alternative direction

SIGNATURES REQUIRED:
N/A

FINANCING:
N/A

   ☐ Airport Authority Counsel:

 DATE:              March 7, 2024

 TO:                Border Coast Regional Airport Authority Board of Commissioners

 FROM:              Ryan Cooley, Airport Director

 SUBJECT:           South Passenger Terminal Door Repairs


INTRODUCTION:
Receive information regarding passenger terminal door.**

SUMMARY/DISCUSSION:
In July of 2023, the right outermost south entrance automatic door gear box of the passenger terminal stopped working properly when
closing. The automatic door opens without issue, but upon closing, the right door closes faster than the left. For safety reasons, the
outer most automatic door has been turned off, turning into a manual door. The door has been operating and functioning as a manual
door since, though the right door closes faster than the left door. A sign has recently been placed on both sides of the door notifying the
public of the manual door operation, the speed at which the door closes and direction to the sliding automatic door located on the east
side of the terminal, should an automatic door be needed for entry into the passenger terminal.

This has been a difficult door to get repaired, due to the nature of the proprietary part involved. Airport Staff has since been working to
get the gear box repaired. We immediately reached out to local businesses like Crescent City Glass to try to get the repair done locally
to keep costs down. Unfortunately, we were advised they do not do work on the motors. The following out of town businesses were
contacted:

    •    Capital Doors – Modesto, CA: Had contracted work out to Redwood Glass and Window for our east entrance sliding doors in
         the past. Unresponsive.
    •    Redwood Glass and Window – Fortuna, CA: Had replaced motor belt on east entrance sliding door in the past
              o July 13, 2023 pictures of the door and gear box were submitted.
              o July 26, 2023 followed up on the status of the repair inquiry.
              o August 8, 2023 received update regarding staff shortage and scheduling issues.
              o August 15, 2023 received quote of $2,750.00. Was notified they were experiencing extreme staffing shortages, were
                   unsure when they would be available.
              o August 18, 2023 Smith River Complex Fire Emergency Starts
              o August 31, 2023 after receiving one unresponsive bid and one declination to bid, approval given to Redwood Glass
                   and Window to proceed with repairs.
              o October 30, 2023 followed up via phone call and email with Redwood Glass and Window, inquiring about the repair
                   status. Unresponsive.

After receiving no further response from Capital Doors or Redwood Glass and Window, airport staff proceeded to move on to the
distributor of the door, Assa Abloy



    •    Assa Abloy – National Dealer of Stanley Automatic Doors
             o November 7, 2023 airport Staff reached out to Assa Abloy, via email and telephone. Was directed to their website to
                 place a service request.
             o November 16, 2023 airport staff followed up on the status of the service request. Unresponsive.
             o November 28, 2023 airport staff followed up on the status of the service request. Unresponsive.

On January 29, 2024 Crescent City Glass and Stay Safe Locksmith were working on a lock on the door, due to a faulty cylinder and
were shown the broken gear box. Both contractors confirmed they do not work on the motors. Stay Safe Locksmith mentioned that they
may have a contact with Stanley Doors and would follow up if they had any information to share. Unfortunately, there was no further
information shared.
After not receiving any response from Assa Abloy, Patty Stanley reached out to Sutter Hospital, as she knew they were the only other
commercial building in Crescent City, CA with these Stanley doors. The maintenance superintendent was kind enough to look at the
door, confirming that the gear box was indeed broken. Airport staff was notified where to buy the parts necessary. As of February 15th,
2024 the gear box operator unit has been ordered and will be installed by airport staff once it arrives.
